query: Consider the following context: The recent perspective of multiprincipal element alloys (MPEAs), also known as high-entropy alloys (HEAs), has emerged as a very promising area for material design. Additive manufacturing (AM) strategies have also been noted to provide additional strength to HEA systems. In the selected dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA system, an additional strength of approximately 300–400 MPa was achieved by adopting an additive manufacturing route as compared to its cast and wrought counterparts. However, the challenge of oxidation degradation always imposes a severe limitation for high-temperature applications in gas turbines, power plants, and aerospace components. Hence, ensuring material sustainability, longevity, and integrity for high-temperature applications inevitably requires the exploration of the oxidation behavior of alloys. In that context, which method can be used for elucidating the mechanistic aspects and elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates on oxidation behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: In-situ (S)TEM combined with advanced elemental mapping (EDS/EELS) and 3D atom-probe tomography on the additively-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy will reveal that high-temperature oxidation leads to local diffusional rearrangements of Al, Cr, and Ti in the nanoprecipitates, producing stable oxide layers that improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy processed via additive manufacturing
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to high-temperature oxidative environments while performing in-situ electron microscopy and atom-probe tomography analysis
generation.conditions: Temperatures ranging from 800 to 1000 °C in an oxidative environment representative of typical gas turbine operating conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale precipitates formed by Al and Ti in the quinary HEA matrix, providing a protective oxidation barrier
generation.mechanism: Dynamic redistribution of reactive elements (Al, Cr, and Ti) toward the oxidized surface forms stable, adherent oxide scales that reduce oxidation kinetics
generation.predicted_outcome: The real-time morphological changes and elemental diffusion pathways within nanoprecipitates will correlate with increased surface oxide protection and improved high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.baseline: Post-exposure characterizations, without in-situ tracking of elemental redistribution, provide limited information on dynamic oxidation phenomena in the HEA
generation.boundary: Results may differ at higher temperatures (>1000 °C) or longer exposure times, where additional phase transformations or oxide spallation may occur
generation.uncertainty: The correlation of measured composition variations to local oxidation rates may be non-trivial, and experimental artifacts in electron microscopy or sputtering in APT can complicate data interpretation

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare cylindrical micropillars from the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA using a focused ion beam (FIB), place them in an in-situ TEM heating holder and gradually increase temperature up to 1000 °C in a controlled oxygen atmosphere, concurrently imaging structural changes. After oxidation, retrieve micropillars for atom-probe tomography to determine local elemental compositions and distributions in the oxide scale and interfacial regions.
measurements: TEM bright-field/dark-field imaging of precipitate coarsening and morphological changes
APT-based 3D reconstructions of the post-oxidation microstructure at the nanometer scale
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no preferential enrichment of Al, Cr, and Ti is observed at the oxide/metal interface and the oxidation kinetics are not reduced relative to conventional analyses, then the hypothesis that dynamic elemental redistribution promoted the formation of protective oxide layers required for enhanced oxidation resistance would be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: This paper utilizes in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD) to investigate the high-temperature oxidation behaviour of CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). We found that (1) Mn is the major oxide-forming element in both vacuum and air environments, leading to the formation of non-protective oxides that deplete the bulk alloy of Mn; (2) no oxides like Cr 2 O 3 , Fe 2 O 3 , or Fe 3 O 4 were observed during the high-temperature oxidation behaviour of CrMnFeCoNi, which contradicts some previous studies on the isothermal oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi HEA. We also analysed and compared the experimental results with thermodynamic calculations by using ThermoCalc version 2022b software following the CALPHAD method. ThermoCalc predicted spinel oxide in a vacuum environment, along with halite oxides observed in experimental results; also, in an atmospheric environment, it predicted only spinel, indicating the need for further investigation into factors to validate the thermodynamic predictions.
